A discrete trait evolving along a tree, with its whole history

Source: R/traits_history.R
trait_mk.Rd

Simulates a discrete character under the Mk model (Lewis 2001): along each branch the state changes after exponential waiting times, with the rates of q. The result keeps every change, in the format of a stochastic character map of phytools (class simmap), so it is the known history against which reconstructions can be compared, for example by tip_history_metrics().

Usage

trait_mk(
  tree,
  q = 1,
  states = c("0", "1"),
  root_state = NULL,
  alpha = NULL,
  edge_rates = NULL,
  rate_classes = NULL,
  class_switch = 0.1,
  root = NULL
)

Arguments

tree

A rooted phylo tree with branch lengths.

q

One rate for every change between states (the equal-rates model), or a square matrix of rates from the state of each row to the state of each column, with the states as names; its diagonal is ignored.

states

Names of the states, when q is one rate.

root_state

State at the root; NULL draws one with equal probabilities.

alpha

Shape (and rate) of the gamma distribution of the rate multiplier of each branch; NULL for none. Small values make rates more uneven among branches.

edge_rates

Optional multipliers of the rates of each branch, in the order of the rows of tree$edge, instead of drawing them with alpha.

rate_classes

Optional multipliers of the rates in each hidden class, such as c(slow = 0.1, fast = 1); classes without names are called R1, R2 and so on.

class_switch

Rate of moving from one hidden class to each other one.

root

Deprecated; use root_state.

Value

The tree, reordered "cladewise", with class c("simmap", "phylo") and, as in phytools::sim.history(): maps, a list with one element per edge giving the time spent in each state in the order they occurred; mapped.edge, the total time in each state per edge; node.states, the states at the start and end of each edge; and states, the states of the tips. Q holds the rate matrix used. With rates varying among branches, edge_rates holds the multiplier of each edge, in the new order of the edges. With rate_classes, hidden holds the same history with the class of each segment, as states named "state|class", with its own maps, node.states, states and Q, and classes holds the class of each tip.

Details

Rates can vary among branches in two ways. With alpha (or edge_rates), all rates of a branch are multiplied by one factor, drawn for each branch from a gamma distribution with shape and rate alpha (mean 1), as in the model that phytools::fitgammaMk() fits (Revell 2024). With rate_classes, the character has hidden rate classes, as in the hidden-rates models of corHMM (Beaulieu et al. 2013): in class k, changes between states happen at the rates of q times rate_classes[k], and the lineage moves between classes at rate class_switch without changing its state. The class at the root is drawn with equal probabilities.

References

Beaulieu, J. M., O'Meara, B. C., & Donoghue, M. J. (2013). Identifying hidden rate changes in the evolution of a binary morphological character: the evolution of plant habit in campanulid angiosperms. Systematic Biology, 62, 725–737. doi:10.1093/sysbio/syt034

Lewis, P. O. (2001). A likelihood approach to estimating phylogeny from discrete morphological character data. Systematic Biology, 50, 913–925. doi:10.1080/106351501753462876

Revell, L. J. (2024). Testing for heterogeneous rates of discrete character evolution on phylogenies. Journal of Evolutionary Biology, 37, 1591–1602. doi:10.1093/jeb/voae119

See also

tip_history_metrics(), trait_rates() for continuous traits, and trait_ou(), which takes the mapped history as regimes (optima and rates that change with the state).

Other species traits: arrival_ages(), as_herodotools(), food_web_rates(), history_rates(), paint_regimes(), partner_turnover(), plot.rate_matrix(), plot_rates(), plot_traits(), rate_matrix(), region_pool(), species_traits(), tip_history_metrics(), trait_bm(), trait_ou(), trait_rates(), turnover_rates()

Examples

set.seed(1)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(10)
h <- trait_mk(tr, q = 0.5, states = c("forest", "open"))
h$states
#>       t1       t2       t3       t4       t5       t6       t7       t8 
#>   "open"   "open" "forest"   "open"   "open" "forest" "forest"   "open" 
#>       t9      t10 
#>   "open"   "open" 
tip_history_metrics(h)
#>     transitions total_nodes prop_transitions last_transition_time stasis_time
#> t1            0           3             0.00            1.0000000   0.7085115
#> t2            0           4             0.00            1.0000000   0.7085115
#> t3            1           4             0.25            0.1435450   0.7085115
#> t4            0           2             0.00            1.0000000   0.7085115
#> t5            0           3             0.00            1.0000000   0.4696704
#> t6            1           4             0.25            0.3535646   0.4696704
#> t7            1           4             0.25            0.3535646   0.4696704
#> t8            0           3             0.00            1.0000000   0.4696704
#> t9            0           4             0.00            1.0000000   0.4696704
#> t10           0           4             0.00            1.0000000   0.4696704
#>     changes time_since_change
#> t1        0        1.00000000
#> t2        0        1.00000000
#> t3        1        0.02466665
#> t4        0        1.00000000
#> t5        0        1.00000000
#> t6        1        0.27902759
#> t7        1        0.27902759
#> t8        0        1.00000000
#> t9        0        1.00000000
#> t10       0        1.00000000
# rates that vary among branches
g <- trait_mk(tr, q = 0.5, alpha = 0.3)
round(g$edge_rates, 2)
#>  [1] 0.14 0.40 0.22 1.87 1.52 0.00 2.22 0.88 0.15 0.03 0.40 1.67 0.29 0.00 0.00
#> [16] 0.46 0.50 0.03
hr <- trait_mk(tr, q = 0.5, rate_classes = c(slow = 0.1, fast = 2), class_switch = 0.2)
hr$classes
#>     t1     t2     t3     t4     t5     t6     t7     t8     t9    t10 
#> "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "fast"
